newsitem.title: GERMANY: Gesamtmetall sees hope in upcoming labour talks.
newsitem.headline: Gesamtmetall sees hope in upcoming labour talks.

text.p: Werner Stumpfe, president of the German engineering employers' federation Gesamtmetall said on Sunday he is hopeful that wage talks in the German state of North-Rhine Westphalia will end amicably, a German newspaper reported.
The Tagesspiegel said in its Sunday edition that Stumpfe, however, still wants metal and engineering union IG Metall to make concessions that would reduce labour costs.
The union has offered to cut two vacation days if employers continue to pay 100 percent sick pay benefits, not reducing payouts to 80 percent of normal wages as many companies are now aiming to do.
But Stumpfe said the offer does not go far enough and that further offers to reduce labour costs are needed.
Talks between employers and unions in North-Rhine Westphalia, which could form a pilot agreement for the industry as a whole, are set to start on Monday in Krefeld.
